blocks.text: Setting up Notion for digital product testers on Mac

Your Mac is your primary tool for quality assurance. Start by installing the official Notion desktop app. Ensure you are running macOS 13 or later. This provides better performance than the browser version. Use the Notion menu in the menu bar to Check for Updates regularly. If you find the app is slow, press ⌘ R to reload the current page. This clears temporary cache issues.

items: Type / to open the block menu for quick insertion.
Press ⌘ P to open the search bar and jump between pages.
Use ⌘ B to bold text for highlighting critical bug steps.
Press ⇧ ? to view the full list of keyboard shortcuts.
Use ⌘ N to create a new page instantly.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to speed up your testing workflow

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It helps you interact with Notion without clicking through menus. When you need to find a specific test plan, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is. It will point to the location on your screen. If you are writing a bug report, hold fn to dictate your findings directly into a Notion text block. This is faster than typing long descriptions of reproduction steps.

A good bug report needs structure. Create a database in Notion to track your findings. Type /database inline to start. Add columns for Status, Priority, and Reproduction Steps. Use a Select property for status labels like To Do, In Progress, and Resolved. This keeps your testing organized. You can link this database to your main project page for visibility.
Practical tips for better test documentation

items: Create a template for bug reports to ensure consistent data.
Use callout blocks to highlight urgent issues that need immediate attention.
Embed your test scripts or API documentation using the /embed command.
Keep your workspace clean by archiving old pages in a dedicated folder.
Use toggles to hide detailed test steps while keeping the page readable.

blocks.text: Managing your time as a tester

Testers often face high administrative loads. You spend a lot of time documenting issues and managing emails. Use Notion to keep your daily tasks in one place. Ask Lazur to set reminders for your daily standups or testing deadlines. This allows you to focus on the actual testing work instead of managing your calendar. Remember that testing activities take up to 35% of the development lifecycle, so efficiency matters.

Many testers make the mistake of creating too many separate pages. This makes searching difficult later. Try to nest your pages under a single project parent page. Avoid using too many third-party integrations if you do not need them. Simple databases are often better than complex ones. Always check your permissions before sharing sensitive test data with other teams.

faq.question: Can I use Notion offline on my Mac?
faq.answer: Notion requires an internet connection to sync your data. You can view pages you have recently opened, but you cannot edit them reliably while offline.

faq.question: How do I add a bug report template in Notion?
faq.answer: Create a new database item, click the template button, and define the properties you need. You can then reuse this for every new bug report.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside the Notion app?
faq.answer: Yes. You can hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur about your screen or hold fn to dictate text anywhere in the Notion desktop app.
